findings.description: Heredoc stripping removes executable shell syntax on the opening line, including redirection destinations and subsequent commands.
findings.failure_mode:
For `cat <<EOF; cat /root/private.txt
text
EOF`, the scanned body becomes `cat <<HEREDOC`, hiding the actual outside-path read. Likewise, `cat <<EOF > /root/probe
text
EOF` hides its outside-path write destination. These runs incorrectly pass contamination grading.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the complete heredoc opening line and remove only the body and terminator. Continue scanning redirections and other commands on the opening line.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: Skipping every absolute word beginning with `/.` also skips valid paths containing dot components.
findings.failure_mode: `cat /./root/private.txt` reads `/root/private.txt`, but its sole path candidate is discarded before `outside()` can normalize and reject it. Adding `/./` therefore bypasses the outside-path contamination check.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize genuine absolute paths before applying exclusions. Restrict any exemption for repo-relative quote-concatenated tails to that specific syntactic context.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: The unconditional `"=" in w` exemption discards valid absolute filesystem paths; Linux filenames can contain equals signs.
findings.failure_mode: `cat /root/private=backup.txt` accesses an outside file but is graded clean because its path candidate is skipped. The previous implementation passed this candidate to `outside()` and flagged it.
findings.suggested_fix: Determine regex or assignment context from shell syntax rather than exempting every absolute path containing `=`. Ordinary path arguments must still reach `outside()`.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: strip_heredocs() is applied to every Bash command before the ABS_WORD path scan, independent of what consumes the heredoc. DEC-0541's rationale ('file text being written is data, not a path the agent reached') holds for `cat > f <<EOF` but not for interpreters reading the heredoc from stdin: `python3 - <<'PY' ... open('/root/hidden_tests/x') ... PY`, `bash <<EOF cat /mnt/grader/tests EOF`, `node - <<JS`, `sqlite3 db <<SQL`. Those bodies are executed, so an outside absolute path inside them is a path the agent reached. The 1.2.0 grader flagged these; 1.2.2+ returns clean. This is the most common pattern by which a model runs multi-line code in a Bash tool call, so it is a realistic false negative in the contamination detector, not an edge case.
findings.failure_mode: A contaminated run (agent reads hidden tests or grader data via an interpreter fed by a heredoc) is graded `contaminated: false` and its row enters the ablation results as a valid trial.
findings.suggested_fix: Only strip a heredoc body when the command word consuming it is a writer (cat/tee with a redirection, or a redirect to a file); keep scanning the body when the consumer is an interpreter (python*, bash, sh, zsh, node, perl, ruby, sqlite3, psql, awk -f -, etc.) or when the heredoc is attached to a command substitution. Alternatively strip only for `<<` directly preceded by `> file` / `tee` forms and leave everything else scanned.

findings.description: HIDDEN_TOKEN = r"HIDDEN|(?<=[/._=-])hidden\b|\bhidden(?=[/_=-]|\.[A-Za-z0-9])" replaces the case-insensitive substring check for Bash commands. It does not match: `find / -name '*hidden*'` or `-iname '*hidden*'` (the neighbouring char is `*`, which is in neither lookaround), a bare argument `ls hidden`, `cd hidden`, `cat hidden`, `grep -r hidden .` (followed by space or end of string), `ls hiddentests` (no boundary), and any mixed-case form such as `Hidden/`, `HiddenTests`, `hidden_Tests` (only all-caps HIDDEN or lowercase `hidden` are accepted; the old code lowercased the value). The header comment still states every tool_use input is checked for `hidden` (any case). Glob probing for the hidden-test directory is exactly the behaviour the check exists to catch.
findings.failure_mode: An agent that globs or lists for the hidden test directory in a Bash command is graded `contaminated: false`; the run counts as a clean trial.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the token-shape idea for prose suppression but widen it: make the match case-insensitive, add `*`, `?`, `[`, `'`, `"` and whitespace/end-of-string to the lookarounds when the command word is a filesystem tool (find, ls, cd, cat, grep, rg, stat, tree), or simpler: apply the prose exemption only inside heredoc bodies and quoted echo/printf arguments and keep the original `"hidden" in low` check for the rest of the command.

findings.description: `if w.startswith("/."): continue` runs before os.path.normpath(). The words `/./root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/../root/x` and `/./etc/shadow` start with `/.` and are discarded as 'root dot-directory' words even though they normalise to `/root/...` and `/etc/shadow`. The justification ('no Linux root holds dot-dirs') does not cover `.` and `..`, which are the root itself.
findings.failure_mode: An absolute outside path written with a leading `/./` or `/../` component is not a candidate and the run is graded clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude `/.` and `/..` components from the skip: `if w.startswith("/.") and not re.match(r"^/\.\.?(/|$)", w): continue`, or normpath the word first and apply the dot-dir rule to the normalised form.

findings.description: after_closing_quote() treats any character before the quote that is not whitespace or one of `=(<>|;&,` as evidence that the quote closes a preceding token. Python string prefixes and bash ANSI-C quoting are such characters: `python3 -c 'print(open(f"/root/{n}").read())'`, `r"/root/x"`, `b"/root/x"`, and `cat $'/root/.ssh/id_rsa'` all make `/root/...` a skipped word. f-strings holding absolute paths are common in model-written one-liners. This is a sibling of the reviewer's verified backslash case.
findings.failure_mode: Absolute outside paths inside prefixed Python string literals or $'...' quoting are not contamination candidates.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an opening quote as closing a glued token only when the character before it is a path/identifier character AND the quote is preceded by a `$`-expansion or path text (e.g. require `before` to be `"`/`'`/`}`/alnum that itself follows a `$` word), or whitelist the single-letter prefixes f, r, b, u, F, R, B, U and `$` as opening-quote contexts.

findings.description: Extends the reviewer's verified item 1 (exponential backtracking when no terminator line exists). The opener `<<-?\s*(['\"]?)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\1` also matches text that is not a heredoc and therefore never has a terminator: here-strings `cat <<< word` (the regex matches at offset 1), bit shifts `x<<y` / `$((a<<b))`, and C++ `std::cout << name` written through `echo`/`printf`/`sed -i`. Any such command with ~20+ newlines (multi-line printf of a C++ snippet, a multi-line here-string) triggers the same unbounded scan inside the trial job.
findings.failure_mode: The grade step hangs on an ordinary non-heredoc command, blocking the trial and the driver's final reap as described in the reviewer's item 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the opener to a shell operator context (not preceded by `<` and not followed by `<`), and replace the lazy nested group with a line-based scan: find the opener with a simple regex, then search for the terminator line with `re.search(r'^\s*' + re.escape(tag) + r'[ \t]*$', rest, re.M)`; if absent, strip nothing.

findings.description: HISTORY_PROBES[0] is incremented only after the hidden/suite_path/repo_name checks did not return, so a command such as `git log --all -- tests/hidden` counts as contamination and not as a probe. If contamination() returns on the first non-null check_value result (its pre-existing shape), every probe after the first hit is also lost. The header documents history_probes as a count of probes seen in the grade.
findings.failure_mode: history_probes under-reports; telemetry consumers comparing arms by probe rate see biased counts for contaminated runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate GIT_HIST at the top of check_value (before the early returns) and, in contamination(), continue scanning all events for the counter even after a hit is found.

findings.description: The new model_missing guard requires `($ph.model_requested | type) == "string" and $ph.model_requested != ""`. When a phase record has model_requested null or missing but a non-empty models_used naming a different model (a resumed session, a pipeline that did not pass --model), the phase is never degraded. The previous key-by-key comparison produced a mismatch in that case. The header still says degraded is true when 'the requested model is absent from a non-empty models_used'.
findings.failure_mode: A phase that ran on a substituted model with no recorded request is rowed degraded: false and enters the per-arm statistics as a clean trial.
findings.suggested_fix: When model_requested is not a usable string, fall back to the suite/manifest phase model (as drift_check does per the header) or emit a distinct degradation reason ('model_requested missing') instead of silently passing.

findings.description: The tool pre-flight checks only `git jq yq python3 awk`. The header documents the rows file being appended under `flock` and `--detach` re-exec'ing under `setsid nohup`; neither is verified. The companion library explicitly targets bash 3.2 (macOS), where `flock` and `setsid` are absent by default.
findings.failure_mode: On a host without flock/setsid the batch passes pre-flight, launches trials and spends money, then fails at the first row append or on --detach, leaving a partially written batch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `flock` (and `setsid` when --detach is given) to the `for tool in …` pre-flight list, or implement an mkdir-based lock fallback.
